content:
If you are also doing the Gen2 upgrade, you will also have 8 M3x4rT from removing the old expansion joints. These are identical to the M3x4rT screws from the electronics covers, except they use the 2mm allen key instead of the T10 torx driver.

I did not realize that these used different drivers when I put them into the bin together, and the allen key screws don't show up on the cheat sheet. This was quite disturbing until I figured out where they came from and confirmed I was using the right ones here.

(Thankfully I put the M3x5 screws back into the hinges so I don't have to worry about those.)
M3x5rT are for the doors. If you put them back when removing the doors, they are still there.

I want to leave a comment here for Prusa, if someone is monitoring these: this is a good example of the need for standardization of these screws. The proliferation of screw types would make sense if this were a product manufactured to be fully assembled in-house. However, the reality of the Prusa community and product release cycle is that user-assembled, user-serviced is the mode that will continue for the foreseeable future.

tl:dr; please pick three or four standard screw sizes and stick to em.
The back of the "thank you" letter has the pre-printed cheat sheet with all of the screw types and measurements.
yeah, it should mention when you take m3x5t off the door hinges, put the screws back in the hinge s so that they do not get confused later.
Uhhhh, I have 12 of these with no distinguishable difference...and maybe none of the others? but maybe the difference in size is so minute it's hard to see. Dammit
